items.stem: You soak seeds of bean and observe them after 2-3 days. What will be your observations?
items.answer: It will be observed that the seed coat becomes soft and gets ruptured. Between the two cotyledons of the bean, the radicle emerges first and this is followed by the emergence of the leafy plumule.
items.ocr: Printed 'radical' read as the botanical term 'radicle'; 'gets ruptured' kept as printed.

items.stem: With the help of a diagram, show the different stages of binary fission in Amoeba.
items.answer: In Amoeba, asexual reproduction under suitable conditions takes place by binary fission. In this process, the Amoeba divides into two daughter cells and each one of them grows into an adult organism. During this, the nuclear division takes place first, followed by the appearance of a constriction in the cell membrane, which gradually increases inwards and divides the cytoplasm into two parts. Finally, two daughter organisms are formed. The diagram shows the stages: (i) parent Amoeba, (ii) nucleus elongating and dividing, (iii) constriction appearing in the cell membrane, (iv) cytoplasm dividing, and (v) two daughter Amoebae.

items.stem: How do the following organisms reproduce by asexual reproduction? (a) Hydra (b) Planaria (c) Malarial parasite (d) Potato
items.answer: (a) Hydra — Budding / Regeneration. (b) Planaria — Regeneration. (c) Malarial parasite — Multiple fission. (d) Potato — Vegetative propagation by stem.
items.ocr: The dashes before the answers of parts (b) and (c) were dropped by OCR and have been restored.

items.stem: What is the basic event in reproduction?
items.answer: The basic event in reproduction is the creation of a copy of the parent DNA. Cells use chemical reactions to build copies of their DNA. This creates two copies of the DNA in a reproducing cell and they need to be separated from each other. For this it is necessary to create an additional cellular structure, so that the DNA copies separate into these two cells.
items.ocr: Printed 'the creation of a parent DNA copy' read as 'creation of a copy of the parent DNA'.

items.stem: What is grafting? What do the terms 'stock' and 'scion' mean in grafting?
items.answer: Grafting is a method in which two parts of two closely related plants are joined in such a way that they grow as one plant. 'Stock' is the rooted plant on which grafting is performed. 'Scion' is the portion of the other plant (bud, branch, etc.) that is grafted on the stock.

items.stem: What will happen when (a) a mature Spirogyra filament attains considerable length? (b) Planaria gets cut into two pieces?
items.answer: (a) If a mature Spirogyra attains considerable length, its filament breaks into smaller fragments and each fragment gives rise to a new filament through fragmentation. (b) If a Planaria is cut into two pieces, each piece regenerates into a new complete Planaria.

items.stem: (a) Trace the path of sperms from where they are produced in the human body to the exterior. (b) Write the functions of the secretions of the prostate gland and the seminal vesicles in humans.
items.answer: (a) The sperms produced in the testes are delivered through the vas deferens, which unites with another tube, the urethra, emerging from the urinary bladder. The urethra carries the sperms to an organ called the penis. The penis passes the sperms from the man's body into the vagina in the woman's body during mating. (b) (i) Seminal vesicles: they secrete alkaline secretions that adjust the pH of the semen and provide nourishment to the sperms. (ii) Prostate gland: its secretion keeps the sperms active and mobile; it secretes a fluid comprising up to a third of the semen volume and assists sperm motility.
items.ocr: The printed solution says the alkaline seminal secretion 'lowers the pH' of semen, which contradicts 'alkaline'; reworded to 'adjust the pH' rather than reproduce the printed error.

items.stem: Variations are important for the survival of a species over time. Justify this statement with reasons.
items.answer: Variations (changes in DNA structure) help individuals to survive even after a drastic change occurs in nature. Accumulation of various new variations leads to the evolution of new species which are more suited to the changed environment. Such changes may be in the niche, temperature, salinity or water level, etc.
items.ocr: OCR dropped the word 'variations' in 'accumulations of various new ... which leads to evolution'; restored from context.

items.stem: Why is DNA copying necessary during reproduction?
items.answer: DNA is the genetic biomolecule which carries genetic information from one generation to another, so its copying is essential for inheritance. Errors in DNA copying lead to variations, which not only give a better survival advantage to an organism but also lead to evolution.

items.stem: Mention the two functions of human testes.
items.answer: The functions of the testes are: (i) to produce the male sex cells or male gametes called sperms, and (ii) to produce the male sex hormone called testosterone.

items.stem: Are the two cells formed in reproduction identical?
items.answer: Whether the two cells are identical or not depends on the copying reactions. No biochemical reaction is absolutely reliable, so some variations occur in the copying of the DNA each time. As a result, the DNA copies generated are similar but not identical to the original. Thus, the surviving cells are similar to, but subtly different from, each other.
items.ocr: Printed stem 'Are the two cells formed in reproduction are identical?' had a duplicated 'are'; corrected.

items.stem: Draw a labelled diagram of the human male reproductive system.
items.answer: The labelled diagram of the human male reproductive system should show: testis, scrotum, epididymis, vas deferens (sperm duct), seminal vesicle, prostate gland, urinary bladder, urethra and penis.

items.stem: (a) Write the full form of DNA. (b) Why are variations essential for a species?
items.answer: (a) DNA stands for Deoxyribonucleic Acid. (b) Variations are important for the survival of a species through evolution, as they allow some individuals to survive changes in the environment.

items.stem: (a) What is vegetative propagation? (b) Write any two advantages of practising this method. Or List two advantages of vegetative propagation.
items.answer: (a) Vegetative propagation is an asexual method of reproduction by which new plants are developed from the vegetative parts of a plant, such as roots, leaves or stems. (b) Advantages of practising vegetative propagation: (i) it is useful for those plants which do not bear seeds or bear very few seeds; (ii) new plants can be produced in comparatively much less time.
items.ocr: OCR damaged the alternative stem ('or st two advantages') — restored to 'Or List two advantages'. The solution printed 'Is a sexual method'; the missing 'a' of 'asexual' restored, and 'produced n' restored to 'produced in'.

items.stem: What are the various methods of asexual reproduction?
items.answer: The various methods of asexual reproduction are: (a) fission, (b) budding, (c) regeneration, (d) spore formation, and (e) vegetative propagation.

items.stem: Leaves of Bryophyllum fallen on the ground produce new plants, whereas the leaves of Jasmine do not. Why?
items.answer: In the case of Bryophyllum, adventitious buds are produced in the notches along the leaf margin; when these leaves fall on the soil, the buds develop into new plants. In the case of Jasmine, no such buds are produced in the notches of the leaves, so its fallen leaves cannot give rise to new plants.

items.stem: What are the disadvantages of natural vegetative propagation?
items.answer: The disadvantages of natural vegetative propagation are: (i) there is less adaptability to the environment since there is no genetic variation, and (ii) the diseases of the parent plant get transferred to the offspring.

items.stem: Which kind of contraceptive method prevents STDs and how?
items.answer: The barrier method (for example, the use of condoms) prevents sexually transmitted diseases, because in this method there is no direct contact between the genital organs of the male and the female and thus the transmission of infection is prevented.
